Painted night river below an ancient Korean stone fortress wall. A full moon's reflection on the river is broken into a thousand trembling silver pieces as the current surges again and again against the wall: waves heave up and pound the stone footings in rhythm, bursting into tall glittering spray, foam flooding over the rocks and drawing back to surge again. Sage-green #8AAFA0 reeds whipped in the rush, cold ice-blue #7EB8F0 moonlight, one warm lamp in a high tower window. Rocking, pounding, surging climax. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
